strongest_counterclaim: The prior conclusion commits an observational-equivalence fallacy: the failure-archaeology sample (n=27, doubly-conditioned on IBD-pullback qualification AND B0 evaluation) is consistent with at least three incompatible mechanisms — (a) eps_preference as a momentum/leadership proxy, (b) eps_preference as a residual earnings-quality filter whose protective effect operated UPSTREAM of IBD screening and is therefore invisible inside this window, and (c) eps_preference as a vestigial feature whose historical lift came entirely from co-loaded variables. The cited evidence does not discriminate between these, and the 'ranking proxy' interpretation is not uniquely supported. The cleaner replacement is not 'swap eps_preference for an EPS-revision factor' but to (i) run a full ablation in an UNCONDITIONED universe, (ii) measure eps_preference against ground-truth EPS revisions at the same snapshot timestamps, and (iii) only then decide whether the slot earns its keep.

attacks.issue: Wrong reference comparison: the numeric_contrasts table contrasts selected_winner medians against false_negative_relative medians, but the relevant test of 'downside-risk control' is whether eps_preference separates false_positive_ruin from selected_winner within is_b0_pick=true cases. The researcher never runs that contrast.
attacks.why_it_matters: If eps_preference IS risk-controlling, the cleanest signature should appear as: ruin cases having lower eps_preference than winner cases within the same B0-pick cohort. By tabulating the wrong contrast, the paper dodges the single most decisive comparison available in the data.

attacks.issue: IBD-pullback conditioning creates an upstream-filter blindness: every name in the archaeology has already passed IBD's own earnings/RS-quality gate. Any downside-protection eps_preference contributes by being even MORE selective than IBD is invisible inside this sample, because those names were excluded before they could become 'false_positive_ruin' candidates.
attacks.why_it_matters: This is a classic Berkson's-selection bias. The 50% ruin rate among B0 picks (8 ruins / 16 picks in the visible sample) is high, but the CONDITIONAL ruin rate given B0 selection is not the same as the MARGINAL effect of eps_preference. To estimate the latter one needs names that B0 evaluated and rejected BECAUSE of low eps_preference, plus their downstream outcomes — neither of which the archaeology provides.

attacks.issue: Post-earnings-announcement drift (PEAD) is a confound that flips the researcher's 'momentum proxy' argument: mom_20, up_day_ratio_20, and elevated vol_ratio_5_20 in the post-event window are precisely the signatures a stock leaves AFTER a confirmed earnings beat. Loading on these features is therefore COMPATIBLE with eps_preference measuring earnings revisions, not contradictory.
attacks.why_it_matters: The researcher treats co-loading on mom/up_day_ratio as proof eps_preference is not measuring earnings, but the empirical literature shows these features are themselves downstream consequences of earnings surprises. The correlation is consistent with eps_preference capturing the right thing via correlated proxies — exactly the situation that calls for an ablation test, not a mechanism claim.

attacks.issue: Sample structure is non-iid and small: 27 cases drawn from a handful of snapshots (snap_d0d57b1e40 alone accounts for 6 cases, snap_71486ed83c accounts for 6), and a single dual-labeled case (entity_6618d3e80c) carries 'false_positive_ruin|selected_winner', demonstrating that the win/ruin dichotomy is unstable for any individual name. Standardized deltas computed on n=5 vs n=11 medians are not reliable enough to anchor a mechanism claim.
attacks.why_it_matters: Statistical inference on rank differences across two tiny, snapshot-clustered samples can yield 'separations' that vanish under bootstrap or under a leave-one-snapshot-out jackknife. The paper's mechanism claim rides on these separations.

attacks.issue: The 'deeper, longer pre-breakout pullback' finding is misframed: the researcher calls survivor-of-drawdown evidence of ranking, but 'the company demonstrated earnings resilience through a 15% correction' IS the canonical earnings-quality / downside-resilience story. The same observation is being used to support opposite mechanisms depending on which label you slap on it.
attacks.why_it_matters: If the observation supports both 'ranking proxy' and 'earnings resilience', it supports neither uniquely. Citing it as evidence for the ranking interpretation only is selection-of-evidence.

attacks.issue: The policy implication 'replace eps_preference with raw earnings-revision breadth' is unsupported: the falsifiable_prediction #5 requires BOTH no degradation in selected_winner share AND >2pp ruin-rate reduction. Failure of EITHER half is supposed to falsify the replacement — but if eps_preference is a momentum proxy (as the researcher claims), the replacement should clearly IMPROVE winners (since it would add real information), making the conjunctive falsifier internally inconsistent with the paper's own mechanism claim.
attacks.why_it_matters: If the paper's claim is right, the conjunctive test should pass on both halves. Constructing a test that can only fail if BOTH halves fail is the wrong design — it should be two independent tests, each capable of falsifying the mechanism on its own.

counterexamples_to_seek: Same-snapshot names with HIGH eps_preference score but located OUTSIDE any IBD-pullback base: if they still cluster with high mom_20 / up_day_ratio_20, the ranking-proxy claim holds; if they do NOT, eps_preference was being driven by the pullback base, not by an independent earnings signal.

Cases within the archaeology where eps_preference is LOW (whatever that means in the data) but the name is a selected_winner: 3 such cases would make the risk-control interpretation untenable and shift weight toward ranking.

Snapshots where the broader EPS-revision breadth for the sector was NEGATIVE: if eps_preference stayed BULLISH in those snapshots and ruin rates spiked, ranking-proxy is supported; if eps_preference correctly turned defensive, the residual-filter interpretation is supported.

B0-rejected (is_b0_pick=false) names with HIGH eps_preference that went on to large_win (entity_05b4c6b1f7, entity_de1c657364 are candidates): if eps_preference was a real risk gate it should have been lower on these, not higher. Document its actual score distribution for this subset.

Cross-sectional check within a single snapshot (e.g., snap_d0d57b1e40, n=6): compute rank correlation between eps_preference and mom_20 within the snapshot. If Spearman rho > 0.6 across names that share macro conditions, eps_preference is at minimum redundant; if rho < 0.3, it carries independent information and the 'pure proxy' claim is weak.

A pre-snapshot earnings-event audit: for each entity, identify whether the trailing 8 weeks contained an EPS release. If 80%+ of high-eps_preference picks had a recent print, the signal is mechanically capturing earnings events — supporting eps_preference, not undermining it.
what_would_change_my_mind: Direct ground-truth: matched PIT EPS-revision-breadth data (e.g., % analysts raising next-Q EPS over trailing 8 weeks) at the same snapshot timestamps as the archaeology. If the rank correlation between eps_preference and this measured variable is < 0.25 across names, eps_preference is NOT capturing earnings and the proxy interpretation stands. If ≥ 0.6, the prior paper's claim is wrong.

Unconditioned ablation: rerun B0 in a universe that includes non-IBD-pullback candidates, then ablate eps_preference. If removing eps_preference changes W4 return of B0 picks by < 0.5pp median AND ruin rate by < 1pp, eps_preference is redundant (consistent with the paper's claim). If ruin rate rises > 2pp, eps_preference was risk-controlling and the prior paper's mechanism claim is falsified.

Within-B0-pick Mann-Whitney on eps_preference score between ruin and winner cases, run with leave-one-snapshot-out jackknife: if separation persists across all jackknife folds (p < 0.05), downside-risk-control interpretation is supported; if it disappears under any fold, the separation was driven by one snapshot's regime, not by eps_preference.

Regime test: split the discovery sample into 'broad EPS revisions positive' vs 'broad EPS revisions negative' subperiods. If eps_preference's lift is concentrated in the negative-revisions regime, it is risk-controlling; if it is uniform or stronger in positive-revisions, it is ranking.

Replacement test, two INDEPENDENT halves (not conjunctive): (a) does the EPS-revision-breadth replacement improve ruin rate by > 2pp? (b) does it preserve selected_winner share within 2pp? Either half failing independently is grounds for rejecting the prior mechanism claim or the replacement, without requiring both to fail simultaneously.
